patch_description:
I took inspiration from the earlier layered entangler programs, but moved away from both the line-based CZ chain and the fully symmetric cube-style mixer. The new design is a compact “butterfly parity transformer”: it alternates shared single-qubit mixers with a three-stage fixed entangling backbone made of long-range CZ links, a CNOT parity fanout, and local CZ recombination.

The key novelty is that the ansatz uses only four shared parameters per block, so every upload/repeat copy stays very parameter-efficient while still forcing noncommuting phase-to-amplitude conversion at multiple scales. This should reduce overfitting, improve generalization, and train faster than the wider seed-style circuits, while still giving enough structured expressivity to fit the binary feature dataset.
